faq.q: What's the difference between gradient types?
faq.a: Linear gradients transition in a straight line from one point to another. Radial gradients emanate from a center point in a circular or elliptical pattern. Conic gradients rotate around a center point, creating a cone-like effect.

faq.q: How many colors can I use in a gradient?
faq.a: You can add unlimited color stops to create complex gradients. However, 2-4 colors typically provide the best visual results for most design purposes. Too many colors can create muddy or overwhelming effects.

faq.q: Can I use the gradients directly in CSS?
faq.a: Yes! The tool generates CSS-ready code with proper vendor prefixes that you can copy and paste directly into your stylesheets. All modern browsers support CSS gradients natively.

faq.q: How do I create smooth color transitions?
faq.a: Use colors that are close to each other on the color wheel, or gradually adjust saturation and lightness while keeping the same hue. Avoid high contrast colors next to each other for smoother transitions.
